issue_request: FHIR-30505 was Published as Persuasive with Modification for OO. It requested an optional repeatable DeviceDefinition.hasPart backbone for device definitions composed of other device definitions, with a mandatory part reference and optional count, and with hasPart reserved for true has-part relationships.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by git commit f662eb0f7a5fe2e8facb3c7eb523bfc132ff50d2, "30503 and 30505", merged by 52550f269ef5b764c6272dc36e68719d1df73cef. That source change added DeviceDefinition.hasPart, DeviceDefinition.hasPart.reference, and DeviceDefinition.hasPart.count along with unrelated FHIR-30503 packaging work.
additional_context: FHIR-32271 later removed DeviceDefinition.parentDevice, kept hasPart, and added hierarchy guidance; it is already represented on the combined branch by commit 92817b8489e9bd2cb6eb4b6701f9d760b4a6d068. FHIR-53301 later renamed hasPart.reference to hasPart.definition[x] and added canonical(DeviceDefinition) plus CodeableConcept choices with aligned example and search-parameter updates. FHIR-39389 supplies broader canonical-resource background but was not separately in scope for this default run.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. DeviceDefinition is active in source/fhir.ini, and current source contains DeviceDefinition.hasPart 0..*, definition[x] 1..1, count 0..1 integer, active has-part-canonical and has-part-code search parameters, an example using definitionCanonical, and notes explaining the component-definition direction. Remaining parentDevice or hasPart.reference strings are inactive comments or migration-map entries.
